title: The Last-Minute Legally Blonde Costume
intro: You do not need a new outfit, you need four things that make it obvious. A hot pink knit over your own jeans, a fluffy pen, a velvet scrunchie and a tiny chihuahua in a pink carrier, and everyone gets it before you say a word. Order it the week of the party and keep the sweater.

sections.heading: Four pieces and your own jeans
paragraphs: This is the costume for the person who forgot Halloween was Saturday. I have been that person. Every piece in the flat lay sits on the floorboards next to a pair of light wash jeans that are not on the list, because you already own jeans. The hot pink sweater, the pens, the dog, the carrier and the scrunchie do all the talking. The jeans just hold your legs in.

The sweater is an oversized knit, so it is meant to hang loose and slouch a little at the shoulders. In the porch photo the sleeves bunch at my wrists and the hem sits just past the waistband, which is exactly the look. Check the size chart on the listing before you order. If you are between sizes, stay with your normal size, since oversized already has the room built in.

Tuck the very front of the sweater into your jeans if you want some shape. Leave it out if there is a buffet. Nobody at the party is going to grade your tuck, but it does look a little more put together in pictures, and you will be in a lot of pictures once people figure out who you are.

sections.heading: The dog does most of the work
paragraphs: The lifelike plush chihuahua is the piece that gets the first laugh. Put it in the pink small dog carrier with its head poking out the front, like in my porch photo, and leave the zipper open just enough. It reads instantly from across a room. A carrier with a tiny face peeking out is funnier than half the actual costumes I saw last year.

The carrier in the flat lay is pink with black mesh panels and black handles, and there are small clips on the sides, so check the listing to see if a shoulder strap comes with it. Carry it by the handles for photos. Your arm will get tired faster than you think, because you will be holding a drink in the other hand all night.

Practical tip from someone who learned it the hard way. Do not leave the dog on a chair. Someone will sit on it, or pick it up and wander off for photos with it, and you will spend twenty minutes hunting for a stuffed chihuahua in a stranger's kitchen. Keep it in the carrier and keep the carrier on you.

sections.heading: Pens, scrunchie and a ponytail
paragraphs: The fluffy pom pom pens come as a three pack. In the flat lay you can see lilac, mint and pink lined up on the floorboards. Use the pink one for the costume, obviously, and hand the other two to friends who showed up with nothing. They are also very good for writing someone's number on a napkin like it is a legal document.

The hot pink jumbo velvet scrunchie goes around a ponytail. In my porch photo it sits low at the back with the ends of my hair falling over one shoulder, which is easy and stays put all night. A high ponytail is more dramatic if your hair is long enough. Curl the ends with a big barrel iron if you have ten minutes. Skip it if you do not.

For makeup, pink lips and a little blush is plenty. Paint your nails a soft pink the night before if you can, because you will be holding that pen up next to your face in every picture. Small gold hoops, like the ones in my photo, are a nice finish if you already own a pair. If not, skip them. Nobody is checking.

sections.heading: Comfortable enough to sit on the steps
paragraphs: Comfort is the best part of this one. You can sit on porch steps, like I did, or on a curb waiting for your ride, or on somebody's kitchen floor at midnight. Flat shoes or sneakers are completely fine. White sneakers look right with light wash jeans, and your feet will thank you around eleven, when everyone in heels starts carrying their shoes.

If the weather turns cold, you are already wearing a sweater, so you win. If it is warm, push the sleeves up to your elbows. The notebook, the glittery iced coffee cup and the potted herbs on the steps behind me in the lifestyle photo are just styling extras. You do not need any of them, although a notebook to scribble in does sell the bit.

When Halloween is over, the sweater goes straight into your fall rotation with jeans and boots. The scrunchie goes in the bathroom drawer and the pens go in your desk cup. The dog stays on a shelf and watches you fold laundry. I am not giving mine back.
